title: Odd Man Out
creator: Carol Reed
place: Crown Liquor Saloon, Great Victoria Street
description: Director Carol Reed’s film about a wounded gunman (James Mason) hunted through the city on his last night. Partly shot in Belfast. Its pub scenes copy the Crown Liquor Saloon, the Victorian gin palace on Great Victoria Street, still pouring today.

title: Belfast
creator: Kenneth Branagh
description: Actor-director Kenneth Branagh’s account of his own childhood in 1969, when riots broke out and his family weighed leaving. Shot in black and white. Branagh grew up on Mountcollyer Street in north Belfast; the family left for England when he was nine.

creator: Yann Demange
description: Director Yann Demange’s thriller about a young British soldier stranded in West Belfast after a riot in 1971, early in the Troubles. Fiction, filmed in England. The peace wall on Cupar Way still separates the Catholic Falls from the Protestant Shankill.

title: Good Vibrations
creator: Lisa Barros D’Sa and Glenn Leyburn
description: Comedy-drama about Terri Hooley, who opened a record shop and label in the 1970s and put out the Undertones’ “Teenage Kicks”. Punk crossed sectarian lines. The Harp Bar on Hill Street, now in the Cathedral Quarter nightlife area, was the scene’s home.

title: Hunger
creator: Steve McQueen
description: Artist Steve McQueen’s first feature, about IRA prisoner Bobby Sands, who starved himself to death in the Maze prison in 1981 aged 27. Hard to watch, with long silent stretches. His mural is on the side of the Sinn Féin office on the Falls Road.

title: The Fall
creator: Allan Cubitt
description: BBC crime series with Gillian Anderson as a London detective hunting a serial killer (Jamie Dornan) who poses as a family man. A rare Belfast story not about the Troubles. Much of it plays out in the well-off south of the city around Malone Road.

title: Kneecap
creator: Rich Peppiatt
place: Cultúrlann McAdam Ó Fiaich, Falls Road
description: Writer-director Rich Peppiatt’s loosely true comedy about Kneecap, a West Belfast hip-hop trio who rap in Irish and play themselves. Crude and political. The Cultúrlann, an Irish-language arts centre on the Falls Road, is a hub of the revival they rap for.
